content: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. Conversely, ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapy. Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. Upon discontinuation of the strong inhibitor, increase the dose to 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. Similarly, ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of darunavir through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring avoidance or alternative therapy. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ketoconazole and darunavir both increase each other's effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole when coadministered with darunavir are not available, so alternative therapies are advised. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration cannot be avoided, administer 500 mg of lapatinib once daily and increase the dose to the indicated level once cobicistat is discontinued. Darunavir similarly increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib and lefamulin via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for therapeutic loss or adverse effects. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of leniolisib, requiring avoidance or alternative therapy. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed an 80 mg daily dose of levomilnacipran if coadministration is necessary. Darunavir may alter estrogen plasma levels, reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (intrauterine) and lomitapide via CYP3A4 metabolism. Lomitapide is contraindicated with cobicistat. Lopinavir decreases darunavir levels by increasing metabolism but also increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Lorlatinib decreases cobicistat levels and effects, while darunavir increases lorlatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg daily and resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for three plasma half-lives. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous lurbinectedin dose. Darunavir similarly increases lurbinectedin levels, requiring the same precautions. Darunavir increases macitentan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Darunavir decreases medroxyprogesterone levels through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid oral formulations. Cobicistat increases mefloquine levels, potentially increasing toxicity. Avoid coadministration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. Darunavir increases metoclopramide (intranasal) levels via CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, as the metoclopramide dose cannot be adjusted. Cobicistat increases midazolam (intranasal) levels, potentially prolonging sedation. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Darunavir increases midazolam levels, contraindicating coadministration due to the risk of prolonged sedation or respiratory depression. Darunavir and cobicistat increase midostaurin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor for increased adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. Mitotane decreases cobicistat levels, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapy. Darunavir increases modafinil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases modafinil levels similarly. Nafcillin decreases cobicistat levels, requiring avoidance or alternative therapy. Darunavir increases nefazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapy. Cobicistat increases neratinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Darunavir increases neratinib levels similarly. Nevirapine decreases cobicistat and darunavir levels, potentially leading to therapeutic loss and resistance. Avoid coadministration. Cobicistat increases nicardipine and nimodipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases norgestimate levels through an unspecified mechanism, requiring avoidance or alternative therapy. Darunavir increases olaparib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Cobicistat increases olaparib levels similarly. Avoid substituting tablets with capsules. Darunavir increases omaveloxolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg daily. Monitor closely for adverse effects. Cobicistat increases omaveloxolone levels similarly. Cobicistat increases ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration. Darunavir increases ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir levels similarly. Avoid coadministration with Viekira Pak. Cobicistat increases osimertinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Darunavir increases osimertinib levels similarly. If no alternative exists, monitor closely for adverse effects. Oxcarbazepine decreases cobicistat levels, requiring alternative anticonvulsant or antiretroviral therapy. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for virologic response loss. Darunavir increases palbociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg daily. Cobicistat increases ozanimod toxicity by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid coadministration. Darunavir increases palovarotene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases pazopanib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg daily. Darunavir increases pazopanib levels similarly. Darunavir increases pemigatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. Cobicistat increases pemigatinib levels similarly. Cobicistat increases perampanel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases perampanel levels similarly. Darunavir increases pexidartinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. Cobicistat increases pexidartinib levels similarly. Phenobarbital decreases cobicistat levels, requiring avoidance or alternative therapy. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for virologic response loss. Darunavir increases pirtobrutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives. Phenytoin decreases cobicistat levels, requiring avoidance or alternative therapy. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for virologic response loss. Cobicistat increases pimavanserin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg daily if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Darunavir increases pomalidomide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases ponatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Cobicistat increases ponatinib levels similarly. Posaconazole increases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases pralsetinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Cobicistat increases pralsetinib levels similarly. Primidone decreases cobicistat levels, contraindicating coadministration. Cobicistat increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases quazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases quetiapine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration with atazanavir and cobicistat in patients taking quetiapine. If necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose and monitor for adverse reactions. Darunavir increases red yeast rice levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially increasing creatine kinase levels and the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is identical to lovastatin. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases repotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Cobicistat increases repotrectinib levels similarly. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases resmetirom levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Avoid coadministration. Darunavir increases ribociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Ribociclib increases darunavir levels similarly. Cobicistat increases ribociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Rifabutin decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir increases rifabutin levels similarly. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Rifampin decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and is contraindicated. Rifapentine decreases darunavir levels by increasing metabolism. Rifapentine decreases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases rimegepant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition.
